content: Tecovirimat can reduce the levels or effects of enzalutamide by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. As tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, caution is advised, and monitoring of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is recommended when co-administered. Similarly, tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of eplerenone, ergoloid mesylates, ergotamine, erlotinib, erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms), estradiol, conjugated synthetic estrogens, esterified estrogens, estropipate, eszopiclone, ethinylestradiol, ethosuximide, etoposide, everolimus, exemestane, felbamate, felodipine, fenofibrate (including micronized forms), fenofibric acid, fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal forms), flurazepam, flutamide, fosamprenavir, fosaprepitant, fostamatinib, gefitinib, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, guanfacine, haloperidol, hydrocodone, hydroxyprogesterone caproate, ibrutinib, idelalisib, imatinib, indinavir, irinotecan (including liposomal forms), isavuconazonium sulfate, isosorbide dinitrate, isosorbide mononitrate, isradipine, itraconazole, ivabradine, ivacaftor, ixabepilone, ixazomib, ketamine, lacosamide, lapatinib, levomilnacipran, levonorgestrel (oral), linagliptin, lomitapide, lopinavir, losartan, lovastatin, lumefantrine, lurasidone, macimorelin, macitentan, maraviroc, medroxyprogesterone, mefloquine, mestranol, metaxalone, methylprednisolone, midazolam, midostaurin, mifepristone, mirtazapine, montelukast, and modafinil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary for these drugs when co-administered with tecovirimat. Tecovirimat can increase the levels or effects of escitalopram, etravirine, fosphenytoin, ifosfamide, imipramine, isotretinoin, lansoprazole, methadone, methsuximide, mavacamten, and modafinil by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2C19. Tecovirimat is a weak inhibitor of CYP2C8 and CYP2C19, and monitoring for adverse effects is recommended when co-administered with sensitive substrates of these enzymes. For mavacamten, therapy modification and close monitoring may be required, as initiating weak CYP2C19 inhibitors may necessitate a reduced mavacamten dose. Additionally, phosphate binders, such as lanthanum carbonate, can increase the levels of tecovirimat by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and caution is advised.
